**I. BIG IDEA: Grammar Conventions** Students observe, analyze, and use the structures and conventions of Standard English grammar, usage, and mechanics as they interpret and construct texts.
**Grammar, Usage, & Mechanics** Draw from knowledge of the conventions of Standard English grammar, usage, and mechanics when analyzing, evaluating, and constructing texts.
**Usage:** Form and use verbals and verbal phrases (participles/participials, gerunds, and infinitives) based on function. (Master)
**Usage:** Use tenses and aspects to indicate the mood of a verb. (Master)
**Mechanics:** Use colons to introduce quotations. (Master)
**Mechanics:** Use dashes appropriately. (Continue)
**Grammar, Usage, Mechanics:** Use an appropriate style guide to address complex issues of grammar, usage, or mechanics. (Continue)

Use knowledge of texts’ distinct disciplinary, personal, or technical purposes to aid comprehension. (I)
Assess the impact of context and language on a text’s reception by the audience. (I)

Construct and self-evaluate multimodal texts and/or presentations that serve more than one purpose and target a specific audience using multiple, clearly identifiable features of incorporated modes. (C)

*Compare and contrast varying perspectives on a particular topic found across a variety of texts, analyzing how texts establish and develop perspective to shape perceptions or beliefs*. (I)
Identify the impact of the speaker’s reliability or credibility on the text. (I)
Synthesize information from a variety of credible sources used to research the answers to questions on academic and individual topics of interest. (C)
**II. BIG IDEA: Structure & Style** Students analyze and use organizational structures and style to shape ideas and information.
**Organization** Analyze, evaluate, and use organizational structures and style to shape thoughts across genres.
Analyze the effectiveness of a text’s organizational structure to meet the needs and expectations of the target audience. (I)
Craft and organize texts using an appropriate structure and features for mode, genre, purpose, and audience. (C)
Guide the audience through texts using transitions between ideas and paragraphs to enhance cohesion. (C)

Apply knowledge of text structure and organization to create coherent and cohesive texts with an introduction that guides the focus and captures the audience; purposefully organized and developed supporting facts, reasons, explanations, details, descriptions, and/or events; and a memorable conclusion. (C)
**Craft** Analyze, evaluate, and craft language to produce intended effects in a wide variety of texts.
Analyze how the use of figurative, connotative, and/or rhetorical language contributes to the development of meaning, tone, or mood in a wide variety of texts. (I)
Use literary devices, figurative language, rhetorical language, and/or rhetorical appeals to create a variety of effects, as appropriate to intended purpose and target audience. (C)
Use formal or informal style, as appropriate to audience, purpose, and context. (C)

Describe how narrative techniques (including archetypes, multiple perspectives, plot structure, and symbolism) interact, using textual evidence. (I)
Analyze how plot structures, conflict, narrative devices, word choice, and other craft techniques are impacted by an author’s purpose. (I)
Analyze how a text’s theme has social relevance and is developed across a text, comparing passages within and across texts, providing both reasoning and supportive textual evidence. (I)
Analyze how literary works draw on themes, event patterns, or character types from different time periods. (I)

Effectively apply a variety of narrative techniques to develop complex character(s) who change, use setting to create mood, develop an idea or theme across the text, achieve specific purposes, engage audiences, and enhance writing. (C)
**Expository Techniques** Evaluate and apply expository techniques to enhance text’s appeal to audiences or achieve specific purposes.
Analyze and evaluate the use and effect of expository techniques and organizational patterns. (I)
Analyze texts with conflicting information or opposing viewpoints and determine where the texts disagree on matters of fact or interpretations. (I)
This progression ends in 5th grade.
**Argumentative Techniques** Evaluate and apply argumentative techniques to enhance text’s appeal to audiences or achieve specific purposes.
Read, discuss, evaluate, and critique a variety of texts, considering the argumentative techniques used to present and design content and their associated implications on meaning or central idea. (I)

Apply argumentative techniques strategically to enhance writing and engage audiences. (C)
Use rhetorical devices and appeals to guide the creation and revision of texts. (C)

Apply knowledge of various poetic techniques and conventions to create poetic text for an intended purpose. (C)

standards.notes: *Comprehension strategies are tools that students should develop throughout their K-12 education as they work to interpret increasingly complex texts. The effectiveness of these strategies depends largely on the texts themselves, the reasons students engage with them, and the preferences and knowledge bases of individual students. For these reasons, students should receive instruction in a variety of comprehension strategies. Students should learn to select and apply strategies flexibly in order to make sense of the text and accomplish their goals.
